comments.text: the game's own start, reached once by the Cyberload boot: jumps over the next vector to the script at $0806.

the one way any part loads a file: A is the file's number (0 to 13, the table at $0912); jumps to $0865, which shows the tape prompt first when the file starts a side and retries the load until it succeeds.

the game's top level. Loads file 7 (TP, the title) and calls it at $8000; then for ever: files 0 and 1 (OC and OM, the menu) and the menu at $1000; the start year's file, 9 + the year chosen ($0389, 0 to 3, so T1 to T4); the map's files 3, 2 and 4 (M2, M1, M3); the year's text ($09EC) and the strategic game at $0C00; then, unless $039B is set, file 13 (CS, the ending) at $8000; and last the prompt for tape 1 side 1 before the menu loads again. The screen is cleared ($09A9) between the steps.
the menu loop's start: clears $037F, then resets the stack to $FF on every pass, so nothing a part left on it survives.
after the strategic game returns: a $039B of 0 loads the ending, any other value goes straight to the prompt for side 1.
the end of a game: asks for tape 1 side 1 ($08CB = 0, the prompt at $092E) and loads the menu again.

stores the file's number in $08CB, quietens the machine ($0898), shows the rewind prompt ($092E) when $0904 marks the file as the first of its side, points $BB/$BC at its two-letter name ($08CC) with the name's length 2 in $B7, and calls the fast loader with mode $41 (load where the file's header says, border flashing). The loader returns carry set on a bad load; the prompt is then shown again and the load retried, for ever.

before a load or a prompt: interrupts off, the KERNAL and BASIC in ($01 = $37), both CIAs' interrupts and timers stopped and acknowledged, border and background black, sprites off, the raster interrupt off and acknowledged, interrupts on again (the KERNAL's).
the number of the file being loaded, written by $0865 (and $085C); read by the loader's caller and the prompt.
fourteen pointers, low byte first, to each file's two-letter name in $0912 (file 0 at $0912, file 1 at $0914 and so on).
file_names, continued: the pointers to files 0 to 13's names, $0912 to $092C, two bytes apart.
the side of the cassette each file is on, 1 or 2, by file number; the prompt shows it.
which of the two cassettes each file is on, 1 or 2, by file number; the prompt shows it.

1 for a file the loader can only find after the tape is rewound (the first of a side the game asks for: M2, S1, S2, BS), 0 for one that follows on the tape from the file before; a 1 shows the rewind prompt first.
the fourteen two-letter file names in ASCII, as the files' headers carry them: OC OM M1 M2 M3 S1 S2 TP BS T1 T2 T3 T4 CS.

the prompt "REWIND TAPE t SIDE s, HIT FIRE THEN PLAY" on the bottom row: quietens the machine ($0898), shows the ROM's upper-case set on a cleared screen ($09CA), writes the tape and side digits from $08F6 and $08E8 into the text ($098D, $0994), copies the 40 characters to $07C0 in white, starts the cassette motor (bit 5 of $01 cleared), waits for fire ($096C) and blanks the screen for the load.
waits until bit 4 of either CIA 1 port reads low, with port A made an output: fire on joystick 2 ($DC00), or on joystick 1, the space bar or another key that pulls the same line ($DC01).
the prompt's 40 screen codes, "REWIND TAPE 1 SIDE 1, HIT FIRE THEN PLAY"; the prompt rewrites the tape digit at $098D and the side digit at $0994.
the prompt text's tape digit, rewritten from $08F6 by $0947.
the prompt text's side digit, rewritten from $08E8 by $093E.
fills the screen at $0400 with spaces and colour RAM with black, then falls into $09CA.
the video chip on bank 0 with the screen at $0400 and the ROM's upper-case characters ($D018 = $14), screen on, 25 rows, no scroll ($D011 = $98), 40 columns ($D016 = $08).

the start year's text before the map: colour RAM red for the first three quarters and black for the last page, border and background black, screen on, the ROM's lower- and upper-case characters ($D018 = $16), so the text the year's file left at $0400 shows in mixed case; then waits for fire ($096C).
73 bytes of $BD between the last routine and the loader, then a jmp $0AAA at $0A60 that no instruction reaches: filler.

the Cyberload loader's entry. A is the mode ($93): bit 0 set loads where the file's header says, clear loads at X/Y (stored into $0B8E/$0B90); bit 1 set returns at once and lets the interrupt finish the load; bit 6 flashes the border; bit 7 compares instead of storing. It switches the ROMs out, points $FFFE at its interrupt ($0ACB) and runs CIA 1's timer A, then waits for the interrupt to set $90 to $FD (done) or $FF (failed) and returns carry set on a failure, with X/Y the end address ($AC/$AD).
the loader's pass-through of a raster interrupt: acknowledges it, interrupts on, and jumps through the vector at $03FE.

the loader's interrupt, one for each pulse on the tape: a raster interrupt goes on to $0AC0; otherwise it reads CIA 1 (the pulse's length against timer A), restarts the timer, flashes the border when mode bit 6 is set, and shifts the bit into $95, branching through the offset at $0AEC, which each state of the loader rewrites.

the offset of the beq at $0AEB, which is always taken (A is 0): 0 sends each bit to $0AED, which hunts for the sync byte $0F; $18 ($0AF7, once it has come) sends each bit to the byte stage at $0B05; $16 ($0BEB, once the load is over) to $0B03, which ignores the pulses.

the loader's byte stage: a byte complete in $95 is added to the checksum $9B and handed to the state the branch at $0B19 names; $0B1A, its offset, is rewritten by every state ($0B28, $0B41, $0B80, $0BA6, $0BD1).

the offset of the bcs at $0B19, the loader's state, stored by each state for the byte that comes next: 0 (the code from here, waiting for the sync byte $0F), $1E ($0B39, the sync), $34 ($0B4F, the header), $6D ($0B88, the start of a block), $18 ($0B33, to $0BB7: the data) and $1B ($0B36, to $0BE1: the checksum).
sync: waits for $0F, then $AA, then clears the byte count $9C and checksum $9B.

the header: its first bytes must match the name asked for ($BB), else the file is skipped and the loader looks for the next; bytes 16 to 21 go to $AC-$B1 (where to load, the length, the pulse timing).
sets CIA 1's timer A from the header's timing ($B0/$B1 times one and a half), the threshold between a short and a long pulse.
the start of a block: unless mode bit 0 is set, loads at X/Y instead of the header's address; takes the next block's length, up to 256 bytes, from $AE/$AF.
the low byte of the address to load at when the mode's bit 0 is clear, the operand of the ldx # at $0B8D, stored from X by $0A66.
the high byte of that address, the operand of the ldy # at $0B8F, stored from Y by $0A69; the code from here takes the block's length and starts it.
stores a byte with all RAM visible ($01 = $04), or compares it when mode bit 7 is set, and steps $AC/$AD; at the block's end goes back for the checksum.
the block's checksum: a wrong one ends the load with $90 = $FF; when the length $AE/$AF is used up the load ends with $90 = $FD.
